title: Retained catalog tombstones shadow current supplier revisions
fault_primitive: Duplicate business-key retirement records precede valid revisions in an existing nonunique MongoDB index
incident_class: Supplier catalog compaction retains tombstones in a collection consumed by a legacy unversioned reader
symptoms: Search and recommendation requests panic in frontend response serialization. Profile RPCs succeed, catalog contains every current profile, and all pods remain healthy. Frontend runtime-error logs surge.
why_hard: No added Kubernetes objects, controllers, collections, or indexes identify the change. Unlike the parent, no profiles are missing: all 80 complete current records exist. Five retained retirement revisions share their IDs and precede them in the existing nonunique index. The profile reader selects one revision without lifecycle filtering and caches it forever. Restoring the existing current records, restarting services, and flushing cache do not remove the shadow revisions. Diagnosis requires correlating successful RPCs, raw cached profiles, and all database revisions for a failing ID.
expected_agent_pitfalls: Treat frontend serialization panic as a release issue
Verify complete current records or hotel 1 and dismiss storage
Restore current records by their original ObjectIds without removing duplicate retirement revisions
Restart profile or flush cache and repopulate the same retired revision
Look for the parent's retention controller or TTL index, neither of which exists
mitigation_summary: Remove retired revisions only when an intact active counterpart exists, remove migration metadata from current rows, then flush memcached-profile. The repair uses only visible cluster data.
